Reviewing billing service ownership checks, notification creation, organization repository, ID generation, date helpers, and potential test breakage.

The spec defines owner role as `organization.ownerId` only. Only that recorded owner may offer or withdraw. Offers target active workspace members excluding the owner. Invalid targets return NotFoundError. Self-offers return "self". One open offer per workspace is allowed. New offers while one exists return "pending_exists". Offers expire after exactly 7 days.

An offer remains actionable until exactly seven days after creation. The status enum includes pending, accepted, declined, canceled, and expired. Withdrawal maps to canceled status. Accepting an offer makes the member the new recorded owner and grants them the owner role; the previous owner steps down to admin if still holding that role at that moment.

Declining an offer clears the pending state and allows the owner to make a new offer. Withdrawal is only possible while an offer remains open. Any workspace member may view the current pending handover via `getPendingOwnershipHandover`. Acceptance triggers a `member.role_changed` event for every role change, including the prior owner stepping down.

Acceptance publishes `organization.ownership_transferred` to TaskflowEventMap with `fromUserId` and `toUserId`. The audit log records this action on the organization. All events during acceptance are emitted on behalf of the accepting member. New member alerts go to the new owner, and billing management rights transfer to them.

A former owner who steps down to admin can be removed like any other admin. The second member with the owner role but not the recorded owner is denied permission. An orgId outside the actor's workspace triggers TenantScopeError. Offers are isolated per workspace. If either party leaves while an offer is open, it withdraws automatically. Refusals throw OwnershipHandoverError with code "conflict".

The refusal reason type is `OwnershipHandoverRefusal` with values "self", "pending_exists", "nothing_pending", and "expired". Only the offered member may accept or decline. Others receive "nothing_pending". This also applies when no offer is open, such as after withdrawal or a second acceptance attempt. Accepting or declining a lapsed offer returns "expired". A lapsed offer is no longer visible, does not block new offers, and acting on it has no effect.

A lapsed offer keeps status "pending" in the database. The system treats it as expired when expiresAt has passed, but does not update the row or set resolvedAt when someone tries to accept or decline it.

A lapsed offer should be marked as expired when a new offer is created. Otherwise two pending rows would exist in the database.

The database row for a lapsed offer will remain pending. The system treats it as expired when reading, but does not update the row on accept or decline. getPending returns null for lapsed offers. The status union includes expired, so it can be persisted if needed.

Withdrawing a lapsed offer returns nothing_pending, not expired. The spec only assigns the expired code to accept or decline actions on a lapsed offer. Since a lapsed offer is not considered open, canceling it follows the same nothing_pending path as an empty workspace.

Reconsidering the error code for a lapsed offer.
